title: Investigating IgAN Through Exploratory Biobanking - The “investIgAte” Biobank
summary:
IgA nephropathy is a chronic kidney disease in which the body's immune system causes inflammation in the kidneys. The course of the disease can vary considerably from person to person. It is still not fully understood why some people experience a faster decline in kidney function than others.
The aim of this project is to collect and store biological samples and health-related information from people with IgA nephropathy for future research. This may help researchers better understand the disease and support the development of improved diagnostic and treatment approaches in the future.
Participants will provide blood and urine samples during their routine medical visits. In addition, selected information about their health status and treatment will be recorded. No additional treatments will be performed as part of the study. Samples and data will be collected over time and stored in a dedicated biobank so that they can be used for future scientific research.

interventions.name: Patients with primary IgA nephropathy (IgAN) are observed within routine clinical practice for up to seven biobank visits. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adult patients (≥18 years of age) with primary IgA nephropathy who are currently receiving treatment for IgA nephropathy or for whom such treatment is planned, who have sufficient understanding of the biobank project, and who have provided written informed consent for participation.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients for whom participation in the biobank project is considered not feasible due to medical or organizational reasons, at the discretion of the treating physician.
